You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router, Prisma/Postgres, separate worker/ process). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/**; API under app/api/**; logic in lib/**; schema in prisma/schema.prisma.

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do NOT touch the live database or live game infrastructure. Do not read .env* files. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-05a-games-freemc.md (Write tool). Exhaustive, factual, cite repo-relative file paths, use tables, mark uncertain items UNVERIFIED. Purpose: 'nothing gets lost' capability safety net.

YOUR AUDIT: GAME SERVERS (paid) + FREE MINECRAFT TIER capability inventory.
Paid game servers: app/dashboard/games/**, components/customer/*game*/*Game*, app/api/games/** (or wherever), lib/games*, worker jobs, the game panel (console/files/mods/plugins/backups/players/worlds/commands/history/schedules/settings/activity), the games catalogue (GAME_META or similar: every game, slug, categories, images, min/max players, RAM recommendations, versions/modpacks, ports, mod support flags), plans/pricing per game, regions, the deployment wizard steps and fields, the /game-servers/mods catalogue page concept (honest: no mod installer exists for paid?), migration-from-X pages.
Free Minecraft: app/dashboard/free-minecraft/**, components/customer/*free*/*Free*, lib/freemc*, api routes; features: power/console/players/settings/presets/rename/change-domain, game modes (12), mod menu, inventory editor, LuckPerms roles/permissions, public server directory, auto-sleep/wake, subdomain routing, limits/quotas, upgrade-to-paid path.
Produce:
1. Data models + status enums + lifecycle for both.
2. CAPABILITY TABLE for paid game servers: action | UI location (file + tab) | API route | backend fn | infra effect | danger level | state handling | reversible | notes. Cover every panel tab and every action, including RCON/console commands, scheduled tasks, backups (create/restore/download/schedule), file manager (upload/edit/unzip), mod/plugin install if any, player management (whitelist/ban/op/kick), world management (reset/upload/download/seed), server properties/settings editor (full field list + schema source), version change/reinstall, startup params, subdomain/DNS, resource meters, activity/history, upgrade/downgrade plan, renew/cancel, delete, transfer.
3. Same CAPABILITY TABLE for free Minecraft (and note what is shared with the paid panel — the settings schema reuse).
4. The games catalogue: full table of games (name, slug, category tags, image assets present, players, ram, mod support, price-from), and where images live; note the 13/19 unlabeled-slug names fix and any remaining inconsistencies.
5. Deployment wizard for games: exact steps and fields, which affect price/region/capacity (required pre-payment) vs changeable later (cite API), the post-payment flow and provisioning states the client can truthfully show (worker job chain + DB status fields + polling endpoint).
6. Plans/pricing source, regions, promos affecting games.
7. Team/permission gating.
8. Gaps: backend capabilities not exposed in UI; UI stubs.
Finish by writing the report, then reply with a ~10-line summary.

/**
 * Host-level capacity accounting for freemc-host — the single shared Docker
 * box every free-tier Minecraft container runs on (see the module doc atop
 * lib/free-minecraft-control.ts for the product's overall architecture).
 *
 * freemc-host is small and FIXED: confirmed live (2026-08-25) at 7.8GB RAM
 * and only 3 vCPUs. recreateGameTypeContainer already assigns each container
 * --cpus (2 for a kind:"plugins" type, 1 for kind:"properties"/vanilla) and
 * --memory (>=2560m for plugins, else the configured free_minecraft_ram_mb).
 * Do the math: this host can run at most ONE plugin-kind server (2 of 3
 * vCPUs) plus one vanilla-kind server (1 vCPU) awake at once before CPU
 * oversubscription — RAM has more headroom, CPU is the binding constraint.
 *
 * This is deliberately NOT a queue system — just an honest "are we full"
 * check the paths we control (create / switch type / manual dashboard start)
 * can consult before starting one more container than the host can actually
 * run. The passive mc-router wake path (a third-party Go proxy that runs
 * `docker start` on its own, outside this app) is explicitly out of scope —
 * we don't control it and can't gate it from here.
 *
 * Plain module (no "use server") — imported from free-minecraft-control.ts,
 * lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts, and lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts, matching
 * the same plain-module convention as ssh-exec.ts and free-minecraft-control.ts.
 */
import type { Client } from "ssh2";
import { exec, shellQuote } from "./ssh-exec";
/** Free-tier container name prefix — see FreeMinecraftServer.containerName's
 *  schema comment (`mc-free-<userId>`) and lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts's
 *  `createFreeMinecraftServer`, the one place that derives it. Every capacity
 *  computation here filters to exactly this prefix so it only ever sums
 *  free-tier containers, never anything else that might run on this host. */
export const FREEMC_CONTAINER_PREFIX = "mc-free-";
export type RunningFreemcContainer = {
  containerName: string;
  cpus: number;
  ramMb: number;
  /** `docker inspect .State.StartedAt`, RFC3339 — empty string if unavailable. */
  startedAt: string;
};
export type FreemcHostCapacity = {
  /** From a live `nproc` on the host — checked fresh every call rather than
   *  hardcoded, so a future host resize is picked up automatically. */
  totalCpus: number;
  /** From a live `free -m` on the host. */
  totalRamMb: number;
  /** Sum of --cpus across every RUNNING (not stopped/exited) free-mc container. */
  committedCpus: number;
  /** Sum of assigned --memory (MB) across every RUNNING free-mc container. */
  committedRamMb: number;
  runningContainers: RunningFreemcContainer[];
};
/**
 * Safety margin reserved for the OS/Docker daemon itself, never handed out to
 * customer containers. Checked live against freemc-host's actual idle
 * baseline (2026-08-25, with every free-mc container stopped except the
 * always-on mc-router): `top`/`mpstat` showed 0.0-0.3% CPU busy (mc-router
 * itself: 0.02% CPU via `docker stats`) and `free -m` showed only ~592MB
 * "used" (out of 7941MB — the other ~2GB "buff/cache" is reclaimable, not a
 * real commitment) for the kernel, sshd, dockerd, containerd, and mc-router
 * combined. So idle overhead alone would justify a far smaller margin than
 * what's reserved here — this is a deliberately conservative buffer on top of
 * that idle baseline, not a measurement of steady-state need, sized for
 * bursty admin/maintenance load this idle snapshot doesn't capture: docker
 * image pulls/plugin downloads, log rotation, cron sweeps, and an admin SSH
 * session running docker/inspect commands like this very check. On a
 * 3-vCPU host, holding back 1 whole vCPU (33%) is a big fraction, but it's
 * simple, easy to reason about, and means the one "spare" core is never fully
 * shared away — better to run one fewer plugin-kind server than to risk
 * starving the daemon that manages all of them. Concretely, with this
 * margin: the host can run ONE plugin-kind server (2 vCPU) alone, or up to
 * TWO vanilla-kind servers (1 vCPU each) together, but NOT one plugin-kind
 * plus one vanilla-kind at once (2+1=3 exceeds the 2-vCPU margined budget) —
 * tighter than the zero-margin hardware ceiling this file's module doc
 * describes, by design.
 */
export const FREEMC_RESERVED_CPUS = 1;
export const FREEMC_RESERVED_RAM_MB = 1024;
/**
 * Live capacity snapshot: host totals + what every running free-mc container
 * has actually been assigned, straight from `docker inspect` (the same
 * NanoCpus/.HostConfig.Memory fields recreateGameTypeContainer's --cpus/
 * --memory flags produce) — never trusted from the DB, since the DB doesn't
